standard.title: Perform learnt and composed music in informal settings
standard.description: sing and play music they have learnt and/or composed in informal settings
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can sing and play in informal settings, follow agreed performance decisions, introduce performances and contribute to post-performance discussion (AC9AMU2P01). They can make basic staging decisions. They have not yet performed from notation in rehearsal/performance, used sound reinforcement technology, or iteratively refined a performance using recordings.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students sing and play music they have learnt and/or composed in informal settings, using notation, staging plans, technology and feedback to prepare and introduce performances.

nodes.label: Performing from notation
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can read from and follow notation or documentation (lead-sheet, staff or graphic notation) when practising and performing music.
nodes.minimum_width: Read from at least one notation format during a rehearsal and apply at least one instruction from it during the performance.
nodes.typical_width: Read from a range of notation formats (lead-sheet, staff and graphic notation) across different repertoire; use notation to guide element manipulation decisions during rehearsal; revise notation when performance decisions change.
wider: Perform from a lead-sheet (lyrics and chords) for a song — navigate the notation in real time and discuss where reading helped and where it required additional preparation
Compare rehearsing from memory vs from notation for the same piece — what are the advantages and limitations of each?
nodes.hinge_reason: Performing from notation is a new performance skill at Y3-4 and the primary new technical demand of this standard relative to Y1-2. Students who cannot follow notation in performance cannot access the full range of repertoire available in Y5-6 and beyond, and cannot participate in ensemble contexts where notation is shared.

response_modes.reason: Reading notation while simultaneously singing, playing and following group cues is a compound skill that requires the notation-reading component to be sufficiently automatic. Targeted practice of notation reading before full rehearsal integration — practise reading the notation first, then add the performance — reduces cognitive load.

success_criteria: Can navigate a notation document during rehearsal and find their place
Follows at least one specific instruction from the notation (e.g. a dynamic marking or repeat sign) during performance

nodes.label: Using technology in rehearsal and performance
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use rehearsal recordings and (with assistance) sound reinforcement to evaluate and improve their performances.
nodes.minimum_width: Make at least one recording of a rehearsal, listen back, and identify one specific thing to improve.
nodes.typical_width: Use rehearsal recordings systematically to evaluate performance and make documented adjustments; with assistance, apply basic sound reinforcement (PA, microphones, foldback) in a performance context and adjust to ensure the audience and performers can hear the music clearly.
wider: Record two rehearsals at different stages of preparation, listen back to both, and document what improved and what still needs work
Learn to set up and adjust basic PA equipment — practise the process before a performance so it is efficient and reliable on the day

response_modes.reason: Listening back to recordings requires students to listen as audience rather than as performers. Build a structured listening framework: 'Listen first for timing, then for balance, then for tone.' Without structure, students either hear only overall impression or listen only for their own part.

success_criteria: Records a rehearsal and identifies at least one specific thing to improve from the recording
Can describe the difference between how they thought they sounded and how they actually sounded

nodes.label: Planning and introducing a performance
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can plan a performance presentation including staging and introduction, and share compositional intent and musical decisions with an audience.
nodes.minimum_width: Plan a performance with at least one staging decision and one introduction element that communicates compositional intent or musical decisions to the audience.
nodes.typical_width: Plan and present performances — introducing using spoken, written or audio-visual formats; sharing compositional intent and how elements of music were used; making staging decisions for the performance space; documenting performance plans.
wider: Present a performance for a specific audience beyond the classroom (e.g. another class, a school assembly) — adapt the introduction format for that audience
Document the full performance plan (staging, introduction, notation, rehearsal notes) as a portfolio — use it to reflect on what worked and what to do differently

response_modes.reason: Performance planning integrates all elements of the standard — notation-guided rehearsal, technology use, staging decisions, introduction format — into a cohesive performance event. The teaching investment is in helping students see that a performance is planned and prepared, not just executed.

success_criteria: Contributes to a performance plan that includes at least staging and introduction
Delivers or contributes to an introduction that communicates compositional intent or musical decisions to the audience
